# Tech billionaires cashed out $16 billion in 2025 as stocks soared. While tech stocks were busy setting records in 2025, the executives behind those companies were equally busy turning their paper fortunes into actual cash — more than $16 billion worth, according to Bloomberg’s analysis of insider trading data. The Amazon founder sold 25 million shares for $5.7 billion in June and July, right around the time he was getting hitched to Lauren Sanchez in Venice. Nvidia’s Jensen Huang watched his company become the world’s first $5 trillion business, and sold $1 billion along the way. Arista Networks CEO Jayshree Ullal cashed out nearly $1 billion as demand for the company’s high-speed networking gear soared and her personal net worth crossed $6 billion. The common thread was an AI-fueled rally that kept pushing tech stocks higher throughout the year. ### Tech billionaires cashed out $16 billion in 2025 as stocks soared. ### How AI is reshaping work and who gets to do it, according to Mercor’s CEO.

[Source 2 — protos.com (Bias: Independent / Unrated)] (URL: https://protos.com/ai-insiders-had-already-cashed-out-7-4-billion-before-stocks-crashed/):
Stated Claim / Post Context:
AI insiders had already cashed out $7.4 billion before stocks crashed

Insiders across nine AI companies cashed out $7.39B across 282 SEC Form 4s long before Thursday’s sell-off.

Actual Article Body:
2:28 PM
							— AI, Nvidia, Stocks				— by Protos Staff

Insiders across nine AI companies cashed out $7.39B across 282 SEC Form 4s long before Thursday’s sell-off.

Insiders at publicly traded AI companies personally cashed out $7.4 billion near peak prices from May through October — right on time. An index of the largest AI stocks, the PHLX Semiconductor Sector, has crashed 32% since its October high.

Since the start of November, this widely-followed AI index has declined 16% and on Thursday, US-listed stocks shed $3.2 trillion in market capitalization in a single trading session. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq 100 index collapsed 6.4%.

Meltdowns were even worse abroad, including a limit-down circuit breaker after South Korea’s KOSPI index crashed 8.5%.

Insiders at AI companies, however, are already sitting on cushy, realized gains.

Across 282 SEC Form 4s from May through October, insiders at nine US AI companies cashed out $7.39 billion. Excluding $179...

[Source 3 — 247wallst.com (Bias: Independent / Unrated)] (URL: https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/08/10/25-year-old-lost-35-billion-of-his-investors-money-2-weeks-later-silicon-valley-insiders-are-lining-up-to-give-him-more-cash/):
# 25-Year-Old Lost $35 Billion of His Investors’ Money. * Aschenbrenner ran 400% leverage on concentrated AI bets including $NBIS and $CRWV, triggering margin calls that vaporized $35 billion in days. * Shorts in $ADBE moved against the fund, yet within two weeks Silicon Valley insiders rallied to offer Aschenbrenner fresh capital. * **Act now:** the analyst who called NVIDIA in 2010 just named his top 10 AI stocks — and Nebius Group didn't make the cut. His AI hedge fund, Situational Awareness, went from a $45 billion peak in early July to about $10 billion by late July after leveraged bets on AI infrastructure stocks unwound in margin calls. Wall Street and Silicon Valley insiders are now asking to hand him more money. On Aug 4, the fund committed a fresh $400 million to an undisclosed private company, on top of a $100 million stake taken the prior month, a $500 million deployment, that reads as his own confidence signal.
